notes: Per-level monster instances from the pristine LEV.ARK. hp is the object's stored hit points (byte 0x08).
combat.attacks[].to_hit_base = attacks[].chance + equip/2 (critter_attack, COMBAT.C:801); damage_base = attacks[].damage + STR/5 (COMBAT.C:799). Powerful adds the ranges shown.
Creature names come from the port's items.h (descriptive, with the item id suffix where the original name repeats); the game's own strings are in STRINGS.PAK, not parsed.

hp is as stored in the file. A critter generated at run time gets avghit * (16 + rand() % 24) / 32 (CREATURE.C:86); hp_authored marks stored values outside that range. The creature table's STR is 0 for every creature in this OBJECTS.DAT, so the STR / 5 damage term is always 0 for monsters.
goal, attitude and old_goal are raw numbers; their meaning is not named in the sources read.

placed_on_map: the monster is on a tile's object chain. Otherwise it is held (via its link) by a create-object trap, item 0x187, which copies it onto the map when it fires; spawn_probability is (63 - trap_quality) / 63 from TRIGGER.C:297. Free-list slots that still hold creature bytes are not counted as monsters.
creature records: passive, remains, armour (255 = none at that location?) and similar fields keep the port's provisional names; see uw1/src/include/critter.h.
